title: PERSONA: A Reproducible Testbed for Pluralistic Alignment

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating how well models align with diverse political views and ideologies by creating synthetic personas and measuring attribute influence via leave-one-out analysis and LLM-as-a-judge preference matching.
Measuring the influence of race and ancestry on model preference alignment through leave-one-out analysis and inter-annotator agreement of models role-playing as diverse synthetic personas.
Assessing model personalization across different age demographics using synthetic user profiles, Direct Principle Feedback, and Cohen's Kappa agreement metrics.
Measuring the impact of the 'sex' attribute on preference extraction and pluralistic alignment using leave-one-out analysis on synthetic demographic profiles.
Leave-one-out analysis evaluating the relevance of religious affiliation to language models' ability to accurately emulate and reflect persona-specific preferences.
Evaluating preference alignment across income, education, and employment status attributes using synthetic personas, Direct Principle Feedback, and critique-in-the-loop LLM evaluations.
Creating synthetic personas with specific disability attributes (including cognitive, vision, and hearing difficulties) to evaluate pluralistic alignment and representation in model outputs.
Evaluating model responses across different household languages, citizenship statuses, and birthplaces using synthetic persona preference datasets and LLM-as-a-judge verification.
